chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the one in Ihram complains of his eyes, let him apply kohl that contains neither musk nor perfume.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on applying kohl for a person in Ihram if it contains musk or perfume?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between general adornments and medicinal use during Ihram, permitting kohl for treating eye ailments provided it is free of musk and perfume. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that prohibitions on 'adornment' (tajammul) do not extend to necessary medical treatments, ensuring the pilgrim's comfort without invalidating the ritual state. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan school of hadith, particularly through Aban ibn Taghlib, in preserving these practical legal details.
